title: Australian Capital Territory (Self-Government) Amendment (Disallowance and Amendment Power of the Commonwealth) Bill 2009

speeches.speaker: Bob Brown
speeches.brief: The member introduced a bill to abolish the Commonwealth executive government's power to disallow or amend any Act of the Australian Capital Territory Legislative Assembly. The bill was agreed to and read a first time.

speeches.speaker: Bob Brown
speeches.brief: The speaker moved a bill to remove the federal executive's power to disallow or amend laws made by the ACT Legislative Assembly, arguing that only the Commonwealth Parliament should have that constitutional authority. The bill would restore the Parliament's exclusive power over territory legislation, referencing the 220,019 voters who elected the ACT legislature in 2008.
